Verdict: request changes. The author is trying to ensure every generated Gradle VERIFY command tests the edited project. The PR improves several paths, but that guarantee still has a hole.

Short answer to your scope question: only computed includes are reasonably out of scope. Nested builds and the misleading fallback are deferred work, not outside the problem described by [issue #219](https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/issues/219).

## Spec

**Act on**

- High: A rejected child project can still fall through to an included non-root parent. [deriveSearchVerifyCommand](/Users/muskanpaliwal/Work/open-source/entire/entire-graph/fix-gradle-verify-project-membership-219/internal/sem/search_verify.go:514) continues walking after [deriveSearchVerifyGradle](/Users/muskanpaliwal/Work/open-source/entire/entire-graph/fix-gradle-verify-project-membership-219/internal/sem/search_verify.go:2021) rejects the child.

  Concrete case:

  ```text
  settings.gradle          includes :parent
  parent/build.gradle
  parent/child/build.gradle
  parent/child/src/main/java/A.java
  parent/child/src/test/java/ATest.java
  ```

  `:parent:child` is correctly rejected, but the walk then emits:

  ```sh
  ./gradlew :parent:test --tests 'ATest'
  ```

  That command does not establish coverage of `parent/child`. This contradicts the PR’s central claim that fallback stops at an unproven Gradle boundary.

- Medium: The repaired rejection path still reports “no build manifest found” through [searchVerifyNoneCommand](/Users/muskanpaliwal/Work/open-source/entire/entire-graph/fix-gradle-verify-project-membership-219/internal/sem/search_verify.go:91). The existing [test fixture](/Users/muskanpaliwal/Work/open-source/entire/entire-graph/fix-gradle-verify-project-membership-219/internal/sem/search_verify_gradle_membership_test.go:33) contains `lib/build.gradle`, and the verbose test confirms the false message. This should say that no safe command could be derived.

**Consider**

- Independent nested-build support belongs to #219. The issue says a directory with its own settings “is a separate build root” and notes that narrow verification lacks a `-p` form. A partial PR may defer that command shape and use `Refs #219`, as [PR #249](https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/pull/249) does, but it cannot treat the issue as finished.

**Noted**

- Computed includes may safely remain unsupported at [searchVerifyGradleSettingsIncludes](/Users/muskanpaliwal/Work/open-source/entire/entire-graph/fix-gradle-verify-project-membership-219/internal/sem/search_verify.go:767). Proving arbitrary Groovy or Kotlin configuration would require executing repository data or building an unsound partial evaluator. Conservative refusal matches the safety contract.

**Dismissed**

- Requiring support for every dynamic settings program. The correct static answer for unprovable membership is no command.

Worst spec issue: the PR still permits an ancestor command that may not test the edited child project.

## Standards

**Act on**

- Gradle ownership policy is split across the narrow walker, suite walker, and root-only guard. That structure caused the missed non-root fallback. The fix should give derivation a way to distinguish “no match here, keep walking” from “this is a Gradle boundary, stop.” Add the included-parent/undeclared-child regression through `buildSearchVerifyCommand`.

- Treat the residual state as unresolved, not absent. Change the generic fallback wording and assert the full output, not only `Tier == "none"`.

**Consider**

- The tests check generated strings but never launch Gradle. One small real-Gradle fixture would anchor the `-p` and project-path assumptions to the external tool’s behavior.

**Noted**

- `mise run check` passed fully in 573.72 seconds, including formatting, vet, build, 164 status-line checks, and the race-enabled suite.
- The focused Gradle family passed.
- No measurable performance regression appeared: 1,000 repetitions took 1.332s on the branch versus 2.079s on upstream main. Repository reads remain capped at 256 paths.
- The review made no changes. `HANDOFF.md` remains untracked.

**Dismissed**

- File size alone is not a new blocker. `search_verify.go` grew from 3,050 to 3,105 lines and was already beyond the threshold.
- A nested directory that is both included by root settings and has its own settings is not automatically a correctness failure. The root project may legitimately use the same directory. That needs a real Gradle counterexample before becoming a blocker.

**Draft GitHub review**

> Request changes
>
> The root and suite cases are improved, but the narrow walk can still escape a rejected Gradle boundary.
>
> If root settings include `:parent`, while `parent/child` has its own undeclared `build.gradle`, rejecting `:parent:child` does not stop `deriveSearchVerifyCommand`. It walks to `parent` and emits `./gradlew :parent:test --tests 'ATest'`, which does not establish coverage of the edited child.
>
> Please add a production-seam regression for that layout and make a declined Gradle boundary stop narrow ancestor discovery.
>
> The residual result also says “no build manifest found” for fixtures that contain `lib/build.gradle`. Please use a reason that describes the actual state, such as “no safe verification command derivable,” and assert that output in the rejection test.

This draft was not posted.

```markdown
## Remaining scope

Independent nested builds currently fall back to an unfiltered suite command such as:

```sh
./gradlew -p modules test
```

The narrow route does not yet add the covering-test filter:

```sh
./gradlew -p modules test --tests 'ATest'

why not fix those here?

The independent nested-build case is fixable here, and there is no strong reason to defer it now. It was originally deferred to keep the safety fix small, not because of a technical blocker.

We can support both forms:

```text
modules/settings.gradle
modules/build.gradle
```

```sh
./gradlew -p modules test --tests 'ATest'
```

And:

```text
modules/settings.gradle     includes :core
modules/core/build.gradle
```

```sh
./gradlew -p modules :core:test --tests 'ATest'
```

The narrow route can reuse the suite route’s wrapper, settings-root, membership, and remap logic. Sharing that ownership resolution would also reduce the chance of the two routes drifting again.

Computed includes are different. A settings file is executable code:

```groovy
file('modules').listFiles().each {
    include it.name
}
```

Static inspection cannot prove which projects this includes without executing repository code and accounting for files, environment variables, plugins, and arbitrary conditions. Guessing would reopen the false-verification bug. Conservative refusal is the correct behavior, not unfinished implementation.

My recommendation:

- Implement filtered `-p ... --tests ...` support in this PR.
- Keep computed includes as an explicitly documented, fail-closed limitation.
- The fallback wording is already fixed.

```markdown
Refs #219

`entire graph search` can suggest a VERIFY command after locating relevant code. Before this change, its Gradle logic could return a command that did not test the edited project.

This branch now requires settings evidence before naming a Gradle project. It also stops suite fallback at unproven Gradle boundaries and supports intermediate build roots whose wrapper lives higher in the repository.

## The bug

The narrow verifier treated a source directory as proof of a Gradle project. Finding `lib/build.gradle` was enough to produce:

```sh
./gradlew :lib:test --tests 'ATest'
```

But a directory named `lib` does not establish a Gradle project named `:lib`. Project membership comes from `settings.gradle` or `settings.gradle.kts`.

For example, this settings file declares only `:app`:

```groovy
include ':app'
```

Given this repository layout:

```text
lib/
├── build.gradle
├── src/main/java/A.java
└── src/test/java/ATest.java
```

the old verifier still emitted `:lib:test`. Gradle rejects that task because the root build does not contain `:lib`.

A project-directory remap is more dangerous:

```groovy

project(':lib').projectDir = file('other')
```

In that case, `:lib:test` can exit successfully while testing `other/`, not the edited files under `lib/`. A passing command becomes a false result.

## Why declining the narrow command was not enough

Command selection tries a narrow test first, then a whole suite, then a build or syntax check.

After the narrow Gradle route declined, suite discovery could continue walking toward the repository root and return:

```sh
./gradlew test
```

That ancestor suite may pass without covering the nested project. The verifier had replaced one invalid command with a plausible but unrelated command.

## What changed

For a non-root narrow command, the verifier now reads the root settings file and requires a literal include for the derived project path. It rejects undeclared projects and projects whose `projectDir` points somewhere else.

Root-project commands still work for both Groovy and Kotlin build manifests. A nearer `build.gradle` or `build.gradle.kts` establishes a nested Gradle boundary, so the verifier does not assume that the root `:test` task covers those files.

Suite discovery now stops when it reaches a Gradle project that cannot justify a command. It no longer climbs past that project and substitutes an ancestor suite.

The suite route also searches from the project directory toward the wrapper for the nearest settings file. This handles layouts such as:

```text
gradlew
modules/
├── settings.gradle
└── core/
    ├── build.gradle
    └── src/main/java/A.java
```

When `modules/settings.gradle` includes `:core`, the verifier emits:

```sh
./gradlew -p modules :core:test
```

The project path is relative to the settings root, while `-p` tells the wrapper which build to run.

| Repository evidence | Result |
|---|---|
| Root settings include `:lib` | Emit `./gradlew :lib:test --tests 'ATest'` |
| Root settings omit `:lib` | Emit no Gradle command |
| Root settings remap `:lib` to `other/` | Emit no command for files under `lib/` |
| Source belongs directly to the root project | Keep `./gradlew :test --tests 'ATest'` |
| Intermediate settings include `:core` | Emit `./gradlew -p modules :core:test` |
| A nested Gradle boundary cannot prove ownership | Do not replace it with an ancestor suite |

These checks fail closed. No Gradle command is better than one that exits successfully without testing the changed code.

The focused Gradle verification family passes:

```sh

```

The tests cover literal project membership, undeclared projects, `projectDir` remaps, root projects, nested boundaries, intermediate settings roots, suite fallback, and command quoting.

The narrow test-class route does not yet support an independent nested build through a command such as `./gradlew -p modules test --tests 'ATest'`.

The settings scanner accepts literal project declarations. It cannot prove membership when a settings script computes its includes dynamically, so those cases produce no command.

The final fallback message can still say that no build manifest was found when a manifest exists but does not provide enough evidence for a safe command.
